job-interview.title: Job Interview Self-Intro
job-interview.subtitle: Introduce yourself at a job interview.
job-interview.culture: In Chinese interviews, a polite nod and a firm handshake are common. Dress a bit more formally than you would at home and arrive about ten minutes early.

dialogue.speaker: interviewer
dialogue.text: 你好，请先做个自我介绍。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐng xiān zuò gè zìwǒ jièshào.
dialogue.en: Hello, please introduce yourself first.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 好的，我叫李明，来自英国。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, wǒ jiào Lǐ Míng, láizì Yīngguó.
dialogue.en: Okay, my name is Li Ming, and I'm from the UK.

dialogue.speaker: interviewer
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu Zhōngwén jīchǔ ma?
dialogue.en: Do you have any Chinese language foundation?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xuéguò yī nián Zhōngwén.
dialogue.en: I have studied Chinese for a year.

choices.text: 我对这个岗位很感兴趣。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhège gǎngwèi hěn gǎn xìngqù.
choices.en: I am very interested in this position.
I have relevant experience.

choices.text: 我希望能在这里长期发展。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng néng zài zhèlǐ chángqī fāzhǎn.
choices.en: I hope to develop here long-term.

office-intro.title: Meeting Your Colleagues
office-intro.subtitle: Introduce yourself and get to know coworkers.
office-intro.culture: Newcomers in Chinese offices are often introduced as 'the new one' (新来的). Colleagues may give you a friendly Chinese nickname, and saying 'ask me if you have questions' is a warm way to start.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 你好，我是新来的，叫杰克。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì xīn lái de, jiào Jiékè.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'm new here. My name is Jack.

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.text: 你好，我叫王芳，坐你旁边。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ jiào Wángfāng, zuò nǐ pángbiān.
dialogue.en: Hello, my name is Wang Fang. I sit next to you.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yǐhòu qǐng duō guānzhào.
dialogue.en: Please take care of me in the future.

words.en: to take care of / to look after

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.pinyin: Bú kèqi, yǒu wèntí wèn wǒ.
dialogue.en: You're welcome. Feel free to ask me if you have any questions.

choices.en: Where is the meeting room?
How do I use the printer?
What time do we get off work today?

words.en: to get off work / to finish work

meeting.title: Speaking in a Meeting
meeting.subtitle: Add your opinion politely in a meeting.
meeting.culture: Chinese meetings often value harmony over open debate. If you disagree, soften it with 我觉得 or 可能, and avoid blunt phrases like 'you're wrong' so nobody loses face.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ bǔchōng yī jù.
dialogue.en: Excuse me, I’d like to add something.

dialogue.speaker: boss
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo, nǐ shuōshuo.
dialogue.en: Okay, go ahead and tell me.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ juédé zhège fāng'àn kěxíng.
dialogue.en: I think this plan is feasible.

dialogue.speaker: boss
dialogue.pinyin: Lǐyóu shì shénme?
dialogue.en: What is the reason?

choices.en: I agree with everyone's opinion.

choices.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yīdiǎn bùtóng de kànfǎ.
choices.en: I have a slightly different opinion.
Could you say that again?

coworker-lunch.title: Lunch with Colleagues
coworker-lunch.subtitle: Join your coworkers for lunch.
coworker-lunch.culture: Eating together is how Chinese coworkers bond. At first people may take turns paying; offering to split the bill (AA制) is also fine and increasingly common among young people.

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ yīqǐ chīfàn ma?
dialogue.en: Do you want to have lunch together?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a, qù nǎr?
dialogue.en: Sure, where to?

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.pinyin: Lóuxià yǒu jiā miànguǎn, hěn piányi.
dialogue.en: There's a noodle shop downstairs, it's very cheap.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Xíng, zǒu ba.
dialogue.en: Okay, let's go.

words.en: particle indicating suggestion or softening tone

choices.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī là de ma?
choices.en: Do you want to eat spicy food?
How's the food at this place?
Is it okay if we go Dutch?

class-questions.title: Asking in Class
class-questions.subtitle: Ask the teacher about a new word.
class-questions.culture: Students in China usually raise a hand politely and address the teacher as 老师. Asking questions after class is common, and teachers are often happy to help.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Lǎoshī, zhège cí shénme yìsi?
dialogue.en: Teacher, what does this word mean?

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Jiùshì “bāngzhù” de yìsi.
dialogue.en: It means 'to help'.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Kěyǐ zài dú yībiàn ma?
dialogue.en: Can you read it again?

dialogue.speaker: teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Dāngrán kěyǐ.
dialogue.en: Of course.

choices.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīngdǒng, néng màn diǎn ma?
choices.en: I didn't understand. Can you speak slower?
Where do I turn in the homework?
What is the exam on?

homework.title: Asking About Homework
homework.subtitle: Confirm what the homework is.
homework.culture: Chinese language classes often require handwriting, since writing characters by hand is seen as part of learning. Homework is usually due at the start of the next class.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, jīntiān zuòyè shì shénme?
dialogue.en: Hello, what's today's homework?

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.pinyin: Xiě liǎng yè hànzì, míngtiān jiāo.
dialogue.en: Write two pages of Chinese characters, due tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Kěyǐ yòng diànnǎo xiě ma?
dialogue.en: Can I write it on the computer?

dialogue.speaker: classmate
dialogue.pinyin: Bùxíng, yào shǒuxiě.
dialogue.en: No, it has to be handwritten.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.en: When is the homework due?
What if I make a mistake while writing?

words.en: write incorrectly / make a mistake while writing

choices.en: Do I need to write the questions too?

library.title: Borrowing from the Library
library.subtitle: Register and borrow books at the library.
library.culture: University libraries in China require a student ID to register, and reading rooms are usually quiet zones. Many have self-service borrowing machines, but asking staff is always fine.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, jiè shū zěnme bàn shǒuxù?
dialogue.en: Hello, how do I go about borrowing a book?

dialogue.speaker: librarian
dialogue.pinyin: Xiān bàn jiè shū zhèng, yào xuéshēng zhèng.
dialogue.en: First, you need to apply for a library card. You need your student ID.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yī cì néng jiè jǐ běn?
dialogue.en: How many books can I borrow at a time?

dialogue.speaker: librarian
dialogue.pinyin: Zuìduō wǔ běn.
dialogue.en: A maximum of five books.

choices.en: How long can I borrow them for?
Will I be fined for returning them late?

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.en: Do you have any foreign language newspapers?

campus-navigation.title: Asking Directions on Campus
campus-navigation.subtitle: Find the teaching building on campus.
campus-navigation.culture: Chinese students are usually happy to give directions and may even walk you part of the way. Pointing with the whole hand, not one finger, is considered more polite.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 你好，请问教学楼怎么走？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐngwèn jiàoxuélóu zěnme zǒu?
dialogue.en: Hello, could you tell me how to get to the teaching building?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, zuǒ zhuǎn jiùshì.
dialogue.en: Go straight ahead and turn left. It's right there.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yuǎn ma?
dialogue.en: Is it far?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng.
dialogue.en: No, it's a five-minute walk.

choices.en: Where is the cafeteria?

choices.pinyin: Tú shū guǎn kāi mén ma?
choices.en: Is the library open?
Which way is the dormitory?

internship.title: Reporting for an Internship
internship.subtitle: Check in on your first day of work.
internship.culture: Interns in China often start with small tasks like taking notes or organizing files. Arriving on time and calling senior colleagues 师傅 or 老师 shows respect.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 你好，我是来实习的，叫大卫。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ shì lái shí xí de, jiào dà wèi.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'm here for an internship. My name is David.

dialogue.speaker: manager
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, xiān zuò zhè biān.
dialogue.en: Hello, please have a seat over here for now.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Jīn tiān wǒ zuò shén me?
dialogue.en: What should I do today?

dialogue.speaker: manager
dialogue.pinyin: Xiān shú xī yī xià huán jìng.
dialogue.en: First, get familiar with the environment.

choices.en: What time do you start work?
Do I need to clock in?

words.en: to clock in / to punch in

choices.en: Is there a work uniform?

business-card.title: Exchanging Business Cards
business-card.subtitle: Exchange cards with a new contact.
business-card.culture: In China, business cards are exchanged with both hands and read briefly before putting them away — tossing one into a pocket right away can seem rude. WeChat is often asked for next.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 这是我的名片，请多指教。
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de míng piàn, qǐng duō zhǐ jiào.
dialogue.en: This is my business card. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.pinyin: Xiè xiè, zhè shì wǒ de.
dialogue.en: Thank you. This is mine.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Guì gōng sī zhǔ yào zuò shén me?
dialogue.en: What does your company mainly do?

dialogue.speaker: colleague
dialogue.pinyin: Zuò wàimào, chūkǒu dào Ōuzhōu.
dialogue.en: We do foreign trade, exporting to Europe.

choices.en: Can I add you on WeChat?
What's your phone number?
How can I contact you in the future?
